clue.text: Such a shocking charge for a blanket!

definitions.text: Such a shocking charge for a blanket!

parts.words: Such a shocking charge for a blanket!
parts.note: a charge that shocks is a current of power, and a blanket heated by mains power carries that same descriptive word

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at a startling price demanded for bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking charge' reads as an outrageous price, but it is the kind of charge that gives you a shock; the warming blanket takes the same adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A current that gives shocks is powered by mains supply, the same word used for heated bedding.

clue.text: Gained attention with end-product

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: a product is what comes out of working on something, here the letters of end reworked

explanation.surface: Someone won notice thanks to a finished article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End-product' looks like one thing; 'product' is the anagram signal, turning END into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Gained as wages or reward, something obtained through work.

clue.text: Need maybe about four for the salad

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the numeral
maybe suggests need could be arranged some other way

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they may want around four for the salad bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' turns NEED into ENDE, which goes round IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy chicory plant used raw in salads, and the word can name the dish.

clue.text: The wickedness of you French, having mine in offensive environment

parts.note: tu is French for you

indicators.note: having means the French pronoun plus the coarse word take the mine within them

parts.note: rude means offensive, here the surrounding setting
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's wickedness, owning a mine in a nasty setting.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT goes into TU + RUDE, between the R and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is depravity, base wickedness of character.

clue.text: Powerlessness of Peruvian ruler pitiably distressed

parts.note: the Inca was the emperor of the old Peruvian empire

indicators.note: distressed means the letters of pitiably are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: An Inca emperor is pathetically upset at his lack of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Inability to act or cope is helplessness, a lack of power.

clue.text: Devices used to gain contract

definitions.meaning: devices here are ruses or dodges
in bridge a contract is made by winning enough rounds of play

explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are crafty devices, and in the card game bridge the rounds won toward a bid share the same word.

clue.text: Bring back wretched dog — he's needed for trimming

indicators.note: bring back tells us the dog word is read from end to start

parts.note: a cur is a worthless mongrel
he, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: Someone recovering a miserable mutt says its owner must groom it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimming' suggests clipping the dog, but it is a frilled strip of fabric used to decorate clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleated or gathered frill sewn onto garments as decoration.

clue.text: Complains about state of transport reserves

indicators.note: about means the grumbling word goes round the state abbreviation

parts.note: to carp is to complain
Ark. is an abbreviation for the US state of Arkansas

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about how the nation's transport stocks are going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of transport' looks like part of the wordplay, but it belongs with 'reserves' in the definition: places reserved for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas set aside for vehicles to be left are parking places for motors.

clue.text: Mistrusts religious groups, including American party-leader

indicators.note: including means the religious groups hold the other letters inside

parts.note: sects are religious groups

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of party

explanation.surface: Someone distrusts religious bodies, one of which counts an American party boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt someone's honesty, to imagine them guilty.

clue.text: Give new instruction about credit arrangement

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word credit means its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A request to reword instructions concerning a loan deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone a fresh order or route is to point them elsewhere with new guidance.

clue.text: Disdains out-of-date material on board

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the stale material sits within the ship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword ship one boards
corn is stale, trite, old-fashioned stuff

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the outdated documents kept on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a committee, but it means aboard a ship, SS (steamship), with CORN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with contempt is to look down on, which is what disdaining is.

clue.text: Roman defence system had changed in all wars

indicators.note: changed means the letters of in all wars are reordered

explanation.surface: A Roman fortification that altered the course of every conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The great stone barrier across northern England built under Emperor Hadrian to keep out raiders.

clue.text: Whereby poem may end in sudden void.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words sudden void

explanation.surface: A poem might finish abruptly in an empty silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across suddEN VOId.
explanation.definitionFit: A short closing stanza addressed to a patron or reader, the traditional way of finishing a ballade.

clue.text: Peyton, for instance, could identify the title

definitions.text: Peyton, for instance, could identify the title

parts.words: Peyton, for instance, could identify the title
parts.note: Peyton is the town in the American TV soap Peyton Place, whose title is made up of a locality's label plus the word for a locality

explanation.surface: Someone called Peyton might be recognised by an honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: Peyton Place was a 1960s American TV soap, also shown in Britain; Peyton reads as a person but is the town in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Peyton is the label of a town, a geographical label, and such a label gave the soap its title.

clue.text: Wear for a feller and …

parts.note: a feller here is not a chap but one who fells trees, and this is the checked coat such a woodsman wears

explanation.surface: Clothing suitable for a man, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like slang for a fellow; it is someone who cuts down trees. The trailing 'and ...' links on to 18 across and does no work here.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman's heavy checked coat is the garment named after tree-cutters.

clue.text: Original model (used by Noah, you say?)

indicators.note: you say means the sound when spoken is what counts

parts.note: the vessel type Noah used would be an ark type

explanation.surface: A prototype boat, like the one Noah sailed, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The first pattern from which copies are made, a prototype.

clue.text: Allotted according to subscription

parts.note: as means according to, as in as agreed
subscription is a signature at the foot of a document, so signed

explanation.surface: Something shared out in line with a membership fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subscription' suggests a fee, but its older sense is a signature written underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Given out as a share or task, apportioned.

clue.text: Publicity man with channels for output

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, a publicity man
ducts are channels for fluid or air

explanation.surface: A publicist with TV channels to fill with programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made are the yield of a factory, its production.

clue.text: … in exchange, for uncle a silver watch

indicators.note: in exchange means the letters of uncle a silver swap places with one another

explanation.surface: Continuing from 14: in return, a nephew gives his uncle a silver timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like the silver gift, but it is a verb-noun meaning close observation.
explanation.definitionFit: Close observation of a suspect is keeping a watch on them.

clue.text: It's to be avoided in an effort to reduce formality

definitions.text: It's to be avoided in an effort to reduce formality

parts.words: It's to be avoided in an effort to reduce formality
parts.note: read as dieting advice it is a carbohydrate to cut out, but stiffness of manner is the formality being reduced

explanation.definitionFit: Stiff formal manner is called this, as is the carbohydrate dieters avoid.

clue.text: Henry's son goes to work for cleansing plant

parts.note: Hy is an abbreviation of Henry, with the 's kept
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Henry's boy starts a job at a purification factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory; it is a herb. 'Goes to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter herb used in Biblical rites of purification, as in 'purge me with' it.

clue.text: Calls for shows

definitions.meaning: a situation that calls for action signals that it is needed
to show is to point out or reveal

explanation.definitionFit: Signalling a need, as symptoms point to treatment, and pointing something out are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Put in order form

definitions.meaning: a form is a school year group

explanation.definitionFit: Sorting into grades and a group of pupils taught together share the word.

clue.text: Income" item in account?

definitions.meaning: an incoming, a way of coming in
each line written in a ledger

explanation.definitionFit: Going in is admission, and a line recorded in a ledger is a bookkeeping record; one word names both.

clue.text: Drink workers make a beeline for

definitions.meaning: the drink of the gods in Greek myth
worker bees fly straight to flowers for this sweet fluid

explanation.definitionFit: The gods' drink in myth and the sugary flower fluid bees collect share the one word.

clue.text: Whistlers' neckwear

parts.note: whistlers are not cheerful people but those carrying whistles, such as referees or sailors, who hang them round the neck on cords

explanation.definitionFit: Cords worn round the neck to hold a whistle or knife, as sailors and officials wear them.

clue.text: Dies out on both sides of America, falling into this?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stand on both sides of the country's letters, enclosing them
out signals the word dies is put out of its usual order

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: Something fading away across the whole of America, sinking into neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' makes DISE from DIES, which goes round US; 'this' is the definition, as things that die out fall into neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that die out fall into neglect, being no longer used.

clue.text: Dismal sort of shot, but sure to pay off

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling dismal
a chip is a short lofted stroke in golf or football

explanation.surface: A gloomy kind of stroke that is nevertheless a safe bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependable share in a top company is reliably profitable, a safe investment.
